minutes.headline: Planning Board sent the medical marijuana bylaw to Town Counsel and backed a DLTA-funded housing master plan element.
minutes.summary: The board closed the continued public hearing on the registered marijuana dispensary bylaw and voted to forward it to Town Counsel. It extended the Highfield Village and 50 Elmwood Road subdivision deadlines, took two new ANR/subdivision plans under review, and heard from the solar contractor about utility poles not on the approved plan. It voted to engage MRPC on a housing element using DLTA funds.

public_comment.topic: Asked what 'all submittals of information' means in the marijuana bylaw and whether every email must be copied to the board.
Urged the board to hold firm against utility poles at the Pleasant Street solar site, arguing underground wiring was in the special permit.
Raised earth removal controls for 50 Elmwood Road, poles on Chase Road, and sewer-driven population projections missing from the master plan.

public_comment.stated_role: Conservation Commission and open space committee member
public_comment.topic: Thanked the board for supporting the Lane property acquisition and announced two site walks.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board closed the continued hearing on the registered marijuana dispensary bylaw and voted to send it to Town Counsel.
The board voted to engage MRPC on a housing element of the master plan, using state DLTA funds.
The board voted to extend the Highfield Village deadline and, separately, the 50 Elmwood Road definitive subdivision decision deadline.
On solar utility poles not on the approved plan, the peer review engineer will research the issue and contact Unitil, and the applicant is to supply drawings.
Staff will send the solar developer a letter confirming electrical work stops until the pole question is resolved.

why_it_matters: The marijuana bylaw is a zoning change, so it is likely to come back as an article residents are asked to vote on at Town Meeting after Town Counsel's review.
The housing element is paid from state funds and a small remaining master plan balance, so it shapes long-term planning for housing without a new local appropriation as described.
The pole question at the Pleasant Street solar site decides whether the project is built as permitted, which bears on how it looks to neighbors.
watch_next: April 28 meeting: the police chief is to be invited to discuss traffic and site distances, and the board is due to vote on the 115 Fairview Road ANR plan in about two weeks.
MRPC is to return in about a month to start the housing element work.

reconciliation.summary: The two records agree on the four main votes (RMD bylaw, Highfield Village, 50 Elmwood Road, MRPC housing element) and most follow-up items, though captions garbled several names. The main difference is who researches the utility pole issue: our minutes say the peer review engineer, the official minutes say the chair.
